utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'll move on with a few matters. The first is the remaining issue from the testimony of Dragic Gojkovic. During the testimony of this witness on the 12th of August of this year, D1171 and D1172 were marked for identification pending a revised English translation for the former and a revised B/C/S original and English translation for the latter. Furthermore, D1183, Gojkovic's expert report, was marked for identification pending agreement between the parties on the parts of the expert report to be tendered. On the 14th of September, the Chamber e-mailed the Defence to ask for an update about these exhibits. On the 8th of October, the Chamber gave the Defence a deadline of one week to update the Chamber. On the 14th of October, the Defence informed the Chamber and the Prosecution via an e-mail that it had uploaded into e-court revised B/C/S and English versions of D1171 and D1172, bearing 65 ter numbers 1D05758a and 1D05759a respectively. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not that I recall, Your Honour. We are checking our records quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I will proceed, meanwhile, and, without giving specific reasons, you may revisit the matter if there are any objections. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace D1171 and D1172 with the revised versions and admits them into evidence. With regard to D1183, the Chamber encourages the parties to come to an agreement as to the excerpt to be tendered and inform the Chamber within two weeks from today. Then the next item would be the delivery of the Chamber's decision on the admission of witness Svetlana Radovanovic's expert report. On the 9th of February 2015, the Defence filed a notice of disclosure of Svetlana Radovanovic's expert report pursuant to Rule 94 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The Prosecution responded to the motion on the 11th of March, not challenging the qualifications of the witness or the relevance of the report, but also not accepting the conclusions of the report and requesting cross-examination of the witness. On the 13th of May, the Trial Chamber allowed Radovanovic to be called as a demographics expert in this case and deferred its decision on the admission of her report until she testified. Radovanovic testified before the Chamber between the 24th and 27th of August. On the 24th of August, her curriculum vitae was admitted into evidence, and her expert report was marked for identification as D1211, under seal. On the same day, the Defence indicated that there were some issues with the English translation of the report. And this is to be found at transcript page 38152. On the 1st of October the Defence informed the Chamber and the Prosecution via an e-mail that the correct English translation of the report had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 1D26-1538. On the 9th of October, the Prosecution advised via an e-mail that it did not object to the new translation. In relation to the confusion with CLSS as raised at transcript pages 40344 to -345, the Defence provided an informal explanation which the Chamber accepts. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of the report with the new translation. Radovanovic reviewed the conclusions of Prosecution experts Ewa Tabeau and Helge Brunborg. The report therefore relates to the charges set out in the indictment and is thus relevant. During cross-examination the Prosecution challenged the witness's methodology and analysis and the scope and accuracy of her sources, the reports conclusions and the arguments used in support of those conclusions. The Chamber considers that these challenges go to the weight that it may ultimately attribute to the witness's evidence, not to its admissibility. The Chamber considers that Radovanovic's evidence may assist in assessing the conclusions drawn by Brunborg and Tabeau. The Chamber finds the proffered evidence to be probative for the purposes of its admission into evidence in this case. Accordingly, the Chamber admits the report of Svetlana Radovanovic, D1211, into evidence, under seal, and this concludes the Chamber's decision. The next oral decision I'll deliver is a decision on the admission of exhibits associated to D982, the witness statement of Nikola Erceg. On 15 September 2014 the Defence filed a Rule 92 ter motion requesting the admission of Erceg's statement and 54 associated exhibits. During Erceg's testimony on the 1st of April, the Defence informed the Chamber that it was, in fact, only tendering only 45 associated exhibits. The Prosecution did not object to the admission of these associated exhibits and the Chamber marked the documents for identification as D983 up to and including D1027. D989, D993 and D1027 have since been admitted into evidence. The Chamber recalls that documents can be admitted as associated exhibits if they form an inseparable and indispensable part of the witness's written testimony. In order to satisfy this test, the tendering party must demonstrate that the witness 's evidence would be incomprehensible or of less probative value without the admission of the associated exhibits into evidence. The Chamber has discussed its interpretation of this case law at transcript pages 530 to 531 and 5601 to 5603, and in its written decisions of the 23rd of July, 2012, and the 7th of February, 2013. The Chamber considers that the information contained in 28 of the tendered documents that the Defence would like to bring to the Chamber's attention is sufficiently quoted in the witness's statement. The Chamber further considers with regard to document D983 that the adjudicated facts in the Karadzic case are not always identical to the adjudicated facts in this case, which may lead to confusion rather than a better understanding of the statement. The Chamber also finds that document D1012 makes the statement less comprehensible. The statement is therefore perfectly comprehensible without these 28 underlying documents. With regard to the remaining 14 associated exhibits, the Chamber finds that their admission is necessary in order to properly understand the witness's evidence. The Chamber therefore admits the following 14 documents into evidence as associated exhibits to the written statement of Erceg: D984 up to D987, D992, D994, D995, D1001, D1007, D1008, D1013, D1017, D1019 and D1026. With regard to the remaining associated exhibits tendered by the Defence, the Chamber denies their admission into evidence. This concludes the Chamber's decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I move to the next item which deals with the remaining issues from the testimony of Mile Poparic. First, Exhibit D1334, during Poparic's testimony on the 5th of November, the Chamber asked the Defence to inform the Chamber by the 12th of November of this year whether or not it relies on the dialogue contained in Exhibit D1334, an eight-minute video of Serbian news footage. This can be found at transcript page 40959. And as of today's date, the Defence has not responded. The Defence is hereby instructed to respond within one day, that is, the response to be -- we will not be in court, is to be received by the Chamber not any later than Monday, 10.00 in the morning, in the way the Defence prefers. Either a short statement Monday morning or by e-mail, which will then later be put on the record. Next one is about D1335. On the 29th of October, 2015, the Chamber asked the Defence to reduce Exhibit D1335, a video of more than two hours, to the portions that were shown in court on the 28th of October. The Defence was asked to update the Chamber within one week, and this can be found at transcript pages 40514 through -515. As of today's date, the Defence has not provided the Chamber with an update. The Defence is hereby instructed to provide the Chamber with an update within the same time-limits as for D1334. Next, D1336. On the 29th of October of this year, D1336, a MUP statement of Huso Palo, was marked for identification pending the verification of its translation. This can be found at transcript pages 40539 through -540 and 40788 through -789. On the 4th of November, the Prosecution pointed out that this statement is part of a larger investigative file uploaded into e-court as document bearing Rule 65 ter number 33373, which subsumes, inter alia, D1336 and Exhibits P614, P615, P617, P618, and P619. This can be found at transcript page 40788. The Defence was instructed to inform the Chamber by the 5th of November of any objections against the admission of the complete investigative file and whether or not it still tenders D1336. As of today's date, the Defence has not responded. The Defence is hereby instructed to respond in court on Monday by 10.00. If you could express yourself already on it, whether you have any objections to the admission of 65 ter number 33373, that is, the whole of the investigative file, please tell us, because then we could decide on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honours, that was our colleague Mr. Lukic's witness, so Mr. Stojanovic and I don't have the knowledge to be able to tell anything useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from you by Monday, 10.00 in the morning. Of course, there's always a possibility to introduce the matter already briefly by e-mail so that it can be put on the record. We move on to D1340. On the 5th of November, D1340 was reserved for an excerpt of a video on shelling and sniping incidents. This can be found on transcript pages 40892 through -893. On the 9th of November, the Chamber received an e-mail from the Defence advising that the surrogate sheet for the video was uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 1D05911A. The Chamber did not receive a DVD containing the excerpts of the video. Could the Defence please provide the Chamber with this CD by not later than Monday morning, 10.00. I take it that you don't have it with you at this moment, Mr. Ivetic or Mr. Stojanovic. Then still in relation to the evidence of Mile Poparic. Further documents and videos tendered by the Prosecution. On the 5th of November, 2014 [sic], the Prosecution submitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I said "2014," I made a mistake because I meant to say on the 5th of November, 2015, the Prosecution submitted via an e-mail a table of investigative source materials related to the report of Mile Poparic and requested the admission into evidence of the documents and videos bearing Rule 65 ter numbers 10020, 10021, 09948, 15704, which is to replace a partial investigative file admitted as Exhibit P7614. I think I have to -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At a later stage, I'll deal with this matter. Please strike from where I said, "On the 5th of November, 2015, the Prosecution submitted via e-mail" because I'll revisit that matter soon. Then I move on to further documents and videos related to Poparic's testimony. On the 5th of November, the Defence circulated a list of 58 documents and videos. The Defence submitted that the number of the documents should be admitted for the purpose of verifying the accuracy of the witness's citations in his report and this can be found on transcript pages 40954 through 40955. The claim recalls its oral decision of the 29th of October, 2012, in which it set out that the Chamber expects the calling party not to tender material underlying proposed expert reports just because a proposed expert referred to or used that document in compiling his or her report. The Chamber therefore invites the Defence to reconsider its position in relation to these documents. The Chamber also will await any formal tendering in relation to documents or videos from the circulated list. I now move to the remaining issues from the testimony of Zorica Subotic. I start with D1270. During Subotic's testimony on the 30th of September of this year, the Defence tendered 1D05545, a MUP report relating to Scheduled Incident G11. However, the document has not been translated and forms part of a larger investigative file which was marked for identification as D1270, pending a response from the Defence on whether or not it objects to its admission instead of 1D05545. This can be found on transcript pages 39514 through 39515 and 39937 through 39938. Can the Defence advise the Chamber within a short time, the 8th of December, if it objects to the admission of D1270 and if it withdraws the tendering of 1D05545. I move on to D1273. On the 30th of September, 2015, D1273, an SRK command letter was marked for identification pending the provision of a better quality copy of the B/C/S original. Could the parties please advise the Chamber if they have located a better copy. Most likely not immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we hear not any later than by close of business Monday, the 8th of December [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, Monday is the 7th. I apologise. That's, indeed, true. It's not within the competence of this Chamber to change the calendar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for the previous D1270, you'd said 8 December. Did you mean Monday or 8 December, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I meant the -- let me give you the benefit of the doubt. You have until the 8th of December. If it was a mistake, you have one day extra.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I now move onto D1265 and D1266. On the 30th of September these exhibits, two videos, were marked for identification pending a discussion by the parties to what extent they agree on what is depicted in the videos and to what extent transcripts of the videos should be tendered. This can be found at transcript pages 39475 through -476. The parties are invited to inform the Chamber of their progress, if any, on this matter. Parties do not have the right to remain silent, but may I take it that you have not made such progress that it's worthwhile to report to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is the kind interpretation of your silence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can give time to my colleagues on the other side who probably know better than I do, since I think this was again Mr. Lukic who would have engaged in such discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what I'm reminded of is that those discussions are ongoing between Mr. Weber and Mr. Lukic, and we expect that they'll be able to report back more concretely. But they're in the process and are assembling the materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That may take a bit more time, so let's be very generous, that we'd like to hear from the parties not later than the 9th of December. Next one, D1278. On 7th of October, D1278, a document containing firing tables, was marked for identification pending a discussion by the parties as to which portions of the document should be tendered and which portions should be translated. May I take it that the parties are unable at this moment to inform the Chamber of their progress, if any, on this matter. And this is not what my text tells me to put to you, but the question was a different one, whether you could update the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Subotic-related documents all fall within the ambit of Mr. Weber and Mr. Lukic's discussions, and so I'd suggest the parties update the Chamber next week on those generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also not any later than the 9th of December. The same would be true for P7567, which is an excerpt from firing tables for M74 120-millimetre light mortar. The same discussion was expected to take place between the parties. The Chamber would like to be updated not later than the 9th of December. I now move on to documents listed as associated exhibits to the 65 ter statement of Dragan Kijac. On the 29th of June of this year, the Defence filed a motion seeking admission of Dragan Kijac's written statement as well as a large number of associated exhibits. Amongst them was a document bearing Rule 65 ter 1D5433, for which the Defence additionally requested that it be added to the Rule 65 ter exhibit list. The request for its addition to the Defence exhibit list is hereby granted. Kijac testified on 19th of October as well as on the 11th and the 12th of November. On 19th October, the Chamber admitted the witness's statement and a large number of associated exhibits into evidence. The Defence did not tender document 65 ter 1D5433 during Kijac's testimony. The Prosecution submitted this document was not admissible as an associated exhibit and expressed concerns regarding its provenance. The Defence did not address or provide reasons for admission of the document during Dragan Kijac's testimony or thereafter. The Chamber recalls that documents can be admitted as associated exhibits if they form an inseparable and indispensable part of the witness's written testimony. It has reviewed the document bearing 65 ter 1D5433 and finds that it does not form an inseparable and indispensable part of Kijac's statement as it does not sufficiently relate to the content of the witness's statement. The Chamber further considers paragraph 12 of the witness's statement to be fully comprehensible and probative without reference to the proposed associated exhibits. Consequently, the Chamber denies its admission into evidence, and this concludes the Chamber's decision in relation to that exhibit. I think a number had not yet been assigned so, therefore, that's everything we'll have to decide. Then I've got three small items left. The first one is a remaining issue from the testimony of Ostoja Marjanovic and it deals with P7636, which is an article from the Balkan Transitional Justice, which, on the 10th of November, 2015, was marked for identification pending the provision of a B/C/S translation. This can be found at transcript pages 41055 through 41056. On the 11th of November, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence via an e-mail that the translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0687-4581-BCST. That same day, the Defence responded, confirming that it had no objection to the translation. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the B/C/S translation to P7636 and admits it into evidence. The next item also is a remaining issue from the testimony of Ostoja Marjanovic. On the 9th of November, 2015, P7632, an article from Balkan Transitional Justice, was marked for identification pending the provision of a B/C/S translation. This can be found at transcript page 41034. On the 10th of November, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence via an e-mail that the translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0687-4583-BCST. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the B/C/S translation to P7632 and admits it into evidence. The Defence has seven days to revisit the matter, if it wishes to do so. The last item on my agenda is a remaining issue from the testimony of Witness GRM-097. It is about P7584. On the 21st of October, 2015, P7584, an excerpt of an UNPROFOR code cable, was marked for identification pending the provision of a B/C/S translation and the upload of the entire document. This can be found at transcript page 40158. On the 13th of November, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence via an e-mail that the entire document had been uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 33311a and that a B/C/S translation had been attached. The Chamber hereby replaces P7584 with the new version and admits it into evidence, assuming that the Defence does not object. However, if you would wish to object, you have an opportunity to do so until the 9th of December. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a quick and small adjustment to what I'll call our concise response to the Court's inquiry about progress on discussions regarding the mortar and firing tables, the Prosecution has, indeed, identified the excerpts for which it will seek admission and provided it to the Defence. Mr. Lukic, in fact, may have already done the same on his part but has been away for this period of time. So I simply wanted to -- I think the same timetable should apply, but I didn't want the Court to get the misimpression that no progress had been made in the interim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, we'll not shorten the time available to further report finally to the Chamber. Any other matter to be raised by the parties? If -- Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just on the two exhibits marked for identification -- or mentioned that had previously been marked for identification from Witness Gojkovic, D1171 and 1172. We have no objection to the translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means -- let me see ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My recollection is the Chamber had admitted them and given us an opportunity to come back, and I was simply putting on the record that we don't be doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1171 and D1172 are admitted. That is -- I think it's with regard to 1183 that the Chamber encouraged the parties then to come to an agreement as to the excerpts to be tendered and inform the Chamber. But D1171 and 72, we now understand that there's no objection and therefore that the decision that it was admitted remains valid. Mr. Ivetic.
